gameModeOther: Depending on the server or player choices the game can be both cooperative and competitive.
analysisDescription: Minecraft is a game that is being continuously updated, so some features can change from version to version. I used to play the game a few years ago, and analysed it with that perspective. For the analysis I consider both a normal multiplayer server with the base game but also some specific servers where the game is slightly changed. Most of the changes I considered were about the creation of mini games. These mini games have specific rules and objectives and sometimes a different player organisation.

dimensionExamples.example: Players usually play with friends. In servers that offer mini-games players can be assign random allies and enemies

dimension.title: Serendipitous
dimension.description: Serendipitous formation happens in games where groups are not defined structures and the gameplay itself (typically proximity) is used to group players.

dimensionExamples.example: The base game has sandbox principles, meaning each player is free to do whatever they want. In som specific cases there can be some sort of end goal like in servers mini-games.

dimension.title: No Goal Structure
dimension.description: No Goal Structure is also a possibility. In some games, the experience in itself is the goal (e.g. simulation games), while in others, the expectation is for player-driven goals to emerge.

dimensionExamples.example: Each player can choose to play the game alone, with friends or even enemies. The game allows for any combinations of progressions, special if the game is adapted to a certain objective.

dimension.title: Individual
dimension.description: Individual progression is defined by individual choice and the individual impact of the progression. In-game activities can vary from individual to fully cooperative but progression affects the individual.

dimensionExamples.example: Each player controls their own character.

dimension.title: Distinct
dimension.description: Distinct means that each player controls a different entity or set of entities

dimensionExamples.example: All characters are the same with the only difference being the customizable skin.

dimension.title: Customisation
dimension.description: Customisation applies when players select their identity by creating or modifying (with a certain degree of freedom) the play style of an entity.

dimensionExamples.example: Players finish the game with their characters equals to when they start. The game's progression is given by items and encantations.

dimension.title: Static
dimension.description: When the player's entity is constant throughout gameplay.

dimensionExamples.example: Players have equal rights while playing the game.

dimension.title: Individuals
dimension.description: Individuals describes when players’ entities have no established relationship with each other, which affects gameplay.

dimensionExamples.example: All players inside a server will play in the same world, and are able to directly affect other players. (If there are no rules)

dimension.title: Shared
dimension.description: Shared world views apply to a game when players have access to the same world.

dimensionExamples.example: The game has the possibility to be played in first person or third person.

dimension.title: Distinct
dimension.description: Distinct refers to when each player has control of their own individual viewpoint, typically through separate screens.

dimensionExamples.example: Players can collaborate with other players or not, since there is no specific objective, the game allows for lots of different scenarios.

dimension.title: Free Collaboration
dimension.description: In free collaboration, players can take on available tasks as they wish and decide how to contribute.

dimensionExamples.example: If two or more players are build a base for instance, they can at different times contribute to it. They can independently gather resources or construct a part of the building and leave. Other player can enter the game and pick were the first player left.

dimension.title: Asynchronous Collaboration
dimension.description: In asynchronous collaboration, players are able to play at different times and still collaborate.

dimensionExamples.example: Players can use the chat to talk with other players.

dimension.title: Agnostic
dimension.description: When Agnostic, the game is neutral to player communication, it does not incentivise nor it places any restrictions. It is the only communication design that does not promote cooperation.

dimensionExamples.example: There is a global chat where players can interact.

dimension.title: Text Chat
dimension.description: Support for players to communicate using text

dimension.title: Grouping
dimension.description: Grouping refers to activities that require a certain number of players to be accessed/completed.

dimensionExamples.example: All items in the world can be used for very player. If there are no pre-deifined rules about it.

dimension.title: Consumables
dimension.description: Consumables refer to items that exist in a limited amount and can be utilised by players to invoke an effect (usually existing as a form of currency, materials, or food) or are not consumed on purpose by players but support the gameplay (e.g., health, energy). Consumables are shared when the agency to consume and manage them pertains to more than one player.

dimensionExamples.example: The game world, although extremely vast, is affect permanently by all the players.

dimension.title: Space
dimension.description: Space is also a resource as it defines the various places in the environment that a player can occupy and interact with. Space is shared when its utilisation is affected or constrained by others' presence or by others’ actions.
